records.reason: An opened session reads as the empty string instead of open, and no reader tells the two apart.
records.evidence: call(path, init) tests the handshake's answer only against 'refused' and 'failed', so the empty string takes the path 'open' takes: the request goes out as asked, read()'s GET or capture's POST with its body, and a 401 renews the session once and repeats that request, body and all. Measured through createApi with an injected fetch and real Responses over a frozen list of 203,979 scenarios: every reader the client returns (me, score, level, streak with its governor, badges, records, feed, insights, insight, wallet and capture) through handshakes that open, fail, drop or are refused, renewals that open, fail, drop, are refused or meet a second 401, and 26 body shapes; and 201,400 interleavings of three callers, capture's POST among them, around a first handshake or a renewal (the second caller 0-24 microtask turns in, the third one turn before it, with it, or one or three turns after it, in either order; the handshake's answer already settled or 0-24 turns late; two calls after every caller settles). Answers, every request (URL, method, credentials, headers and body bytes), handshake counts and launch-data reads were identical to the unmutated client in every one; the two clients differ in no microtask count either.

records.reason: A refused session stays cached, so a later call answers reopen and sends nothing whether or not this sets stopped.
records.evidence: opening() keeps the refused handshake as the session, and nothing clears it: call(path, init) clears session only after a failed handshake, or after a 401 on the open session it used itself, never after a refused one, so no later call, read()'s GET or capture's POST, a first send or a renewal's repeat, can open a second handshake after a refusal. The next call awaits the same settled 'refused' and answers 'reopen' before any send, as it does when stopped is set. Measured through createApi with an injected fetch and real Responses over a frozen list of 203,979 scenarios: every reader the client returns (me, score, level, streak with its governor, badges, records, feed, insights, insight, wallet and capture) through handshakes that open, fail, drop or are refused, renewals that open, fail, drop, are refused or meet a second 401, and 26 body shapes; and 201,400 interleavings of three callers, capture's POST among them, around a first handshake or a renewal (the second caller 0-24 microtask turns in, the third one turn before it, with it, or one or three turns after it, in either order; the handshake's answer already settled or 0-24 turns late; two calls after every caller settles). Answers, every request (URL, method, credentials, headers and body bytes), handshake counts and launch-data reads were identical to the unmutated client in every one; only the number of microtasks a later call takes to answer differs, in 75,284 of them, which is scheduling and not an answer.

records.reason: parseMe, parseScore and parseFeed read an undefined body as they read null.
records.evidence: read() serves every GET reader, and a body json() cannot parse reaches the parser as undefined instead of null; each parser read() is given treats the two alike. parseMe, parseWallet, parseListings and parseEnvelope test for a non-null object, which neither is, and parseScore, parseLevel, parseStreak, parseGovernor, parseBadges, parseRecords and parseFeed read body ?? {}, so both read as a body with none of their fields: each answers null, and insight() maps parseEnvelope's undefined to unavailable alike. capture's POST parses its own response outside read(), so this catch is not on its path. Measured through createApi with an injected fetch and real Responses over a frozen list of 203,979 scenarios: every reader the client returns (me, score, level, streak with its governor, badges, records, feed, insights, insight, wallet and capture) through handshakes that open, fail, drop or are refused, renewals that open, fail, drop, are refused or meet a second 401, and 26 body shapes; and 201,400 interleavings of three callers, capture's POST among them, around a first handshake or a renewal (the second caller 0-24 microtask turns in, the third one turn before it, with it, or one or three turns after it, in either order; the handshake's answer already settled or 0-24 turns late; two calls after every caller settles). Each reader met a 200 or 201 answer with a malformed body or none, streak's governor too: answers, every request (URL, method, credentials, headers and body bytes), handshake counts and launch-data reads were identical to the unmutated client in every one, and so were the microtask counts.

records.reason: A JSON value that is no object reads no study_day either, so null is the one value the object test's neighbour must stop.
records.evidence: A parsed JSON body is null, a boolean, a number, a string, an array or an object; body !== null already stops null, and reading study_day from a boolean, number or string gives undefined, which the string check after it refuses. Only a Fetch body that json() cannot produce (a function) or a polluted Object, String or Number prototype could carry the property. parseMe serves me() alone, through read() and the GET of call(path, init), a first send and a renewal's repeat alike: the frozen list of 203,979 scenarios sent it null, 5, 0, true, false, three strings, two arrays, an empty object, objects with a null, malformed or valid study_day, malformed JSON and no body, at 200 and after renewals, and met it in 201,400 interleavings of three callers: answers, every request, handshake counts and launch-data reads were identical to the unmutated client, and so were the microtask counts.

records.reason: Parsing a launch that has no data as the text null finds no start parameter, the same null.
records.evidence: new URLSearchParams(null) parses the text 'null' into one key called null, so get('start_param') gives null exactly as the guard's own branch does; the only difference a test could see is a stubbed URLSearchParams constructor counting its calls, which is not the wrapper's behaviour. Measured over 32 hosts (none, no Telegram, no WebApp, a WebApp with no initData, and 14 initData texts, the empty one among them, each at Bot API 6.0 and 8.0): every field the wrapper exposes, and the launch data it hands createApi as the handshake in call(path, init) reads and posts it, were identical to the unmutated wrapper; only the stubbed constructor's count differs, on the 6 hosts with no launch data. The start parameter is read once, in the wrapper's constructor, so call()'s POST and renewal paths never reach it.

records.reason: A body that is no plain object holds none of the keys the callers read, so the key tests after record() refuse it whether or not record() does.
records.evidence: Every caller reads only named keys from what record() returns and then tests those keys' own types, and a parsed JSON body that is no plain object (null, a boolean, a number, a string or an array) has none of those keys, so each such value is refused by the key test after it exactly as record() refuses it here.

records.anchor: return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 ? value : null;
records.reason: Number.isInteger already answers false for every value that is not a number.
records.evidence: Number.isInteger(x) is false for a string, boolean, null, undefined, object or array, so dropping the typeof test changes no answer of count().
